notesStmt.note: Whitman's note at the top of this draft indicates that he sent the poem to the New York Herald on March 8, 1888, although the emperor of the title, William I of Germany, did not die until March 9. The letter fragment on the back is dated 17 January 1888, so Whitman must have written this manuscript sometime between late January and early March 1888.

note.p: "The Dead Emperor" was published in the 10 May 1888 issue of the New York Herald and was reprinted later that year in November Boughs.

lg.head: The Dead Emperor
lg.l:
With bending head and eyes, thou too
Columbia

Less for for the mighty crown laid low ‸in sorrow—
less for the Emperor,

A Thy true condolence bringest sendest mourning breathest out
o'er the ‸ salt seas, afar many a salt sea mile,
mourning,
A The mourning a good old man — the a faithful shepherd, ——a patriot,—natural
